verified_behaviors: Management and review requests commit intent before POST and acceptance before status waiting across independent database sessions; separate dialogue turns keep retry count zero.
Worker orchestration uses the real adapter and real finalization database path; intent, idempotency key, local session and submitted Hermes remote session reference agree.

Fresh Python process reconstructs original persisted references and performs only a read-only Hermes GET; no send/resume occurs, query does not mutate attempt, and unknown outcome can later reconcile to explicit terminal status while host failure remains retained.
Runtime resource/host/version/Person/employee ownership changes and changed membership/company scope prevent querying replacement credentials/runtime.

Explicit same-request retries preserve request input digest, use a new attempt/idempotency key, and increment technical_retry_count independently of task rework count; uncertain remote attempts cannot be blindly retried.

Duplicate, out-of-order, late, malformed and secret-bearing telemetry does not write Task/Review/Decision business state or retain prompts/tool args/hidden reasoning/token fragments; unknown usage never becomes zero.
Observation reads use historical company scope, pagination is bounded to 100, seven-day expiry is enforced on reads, pruning is bounded and preserves durable attempts.

Both real adapters stop before waiting when acceptance persistence callback fails; host outcome-write failures retain primary cancellation/error and required cleanup/finalization, with safe disclosure and no claimed receipt.
OpenClaw unknown/missing terminal and Hermes EOF/unknown completion-shaped event never become success; raw OpenClaw operation errors expose only a fixed structured reason.
v56 upgrade/down/upgrade, metadata parity, alembic check, single head, old snapshots and NULL retry history; downgrade refuses populated attempt history before destructive DDL.

Original WorkSession identity/runtime-ref/end/target guards remain intact; new SQL guards reject partial acceptance/host tuples, unreferenced remote terminal claims, attempt identity rewrites and deletion.

contract.request_digest: Canonical host input prompt + declared rendering/runtime context + stable session/request/runtime identity; not a byte-for-byte transport framing or transient-timeout claim.
contract.legacy: WorkSession.technical_retry_count is NULL for historical rows and initialized to zero only in normal create_work_session; original runtime_session_ref remains the once-only local identity.
contract.unknown: Unknown is nonterminal; ended_at and terminal_source remain absent until explicit remote outcome. Host outcome/reason/time is independent and write-once.
contract.retention: Durable attempt history retained; telemetry expires after seven days, bounded prune of 100 runs on writes and explicit prune supports bounded batches up to 1000.
